why: A record whose subject is that NOBODY WALKED, and which is fresh in both halves of the key so that nothing else can be what refuses it. All three hashes here are this point's own, so the grid clause and the ways clause both compare equal and the refusal reaches the verdict — which is the whole point of the probe, because a stale record refuses with this same code while demonstrating a different rule. `verdict` used to be a closed set of two, `passed` and `findings`, and both of them open *the whole was walked*: an author recording an abandoned walk, a walk cut short, or a build stood up and taken down had no legal way to say so and chose which false sentence to sign. The truth could go only into `findings[]`, which is free prose no check reads, so a record saying NO HUMAN WALKED THIS BUILD in its first finding was admitted the moment its verdict said `passed`, and detail work began on a whole nobody had stood in. `unwalked` is that missing value, and this probe is the demonstration that the engine refuses on the FIELD: the `findings[]` here is empty, so nothing but the verdict can be carrying the fact. It declares no unit: every field these documents use is written in the site-plan overlay and compiles there, so there is nothing to exempt — what must not compile is detail work standing on a record that says the walk never happened.
